title: H. pylori Eradication
subtitle: Dyspepsia, epigastric pain — triple/quadruple therapy
content:
[DIAGNOSIS]
- Functional dyspepsia unresponsive to PPI
- Gastric / duodenal ulcer
- MALT lymphoma
- Test: urea breath test, stool Ag, or endoscopy biopsy

[INVESTIGATIONS]
- Culture: Urea breath test (UBT) or stool H. pylori antigen — confirm eradication post-treatment
- Special test: Endoscopy with biopsy if alarm features or refractory dyspepsia
- Lab: CBC (iron deficiency from chronic gastritis), FBS if on long-term PPI
- Monitor: Confirm eradication 4+ weeks after completing therapy

[TREATMENT]
- First-line: Bismuth Quadruple Therapy (14 days)
- Second-line: Levofloxacin Triple Therapy (14 days)
- Third-line: Standard Triple Therapy (14 days)
- Clarithromycin resistance now exceeds 20-30% in many regions

[WARNING]
PPI is essential in all regimens — raises gastric pH and improves antibiotic efficacy. Always confirm eradication 4+ weeks after treatment completion.

[RX-Protocol 1 — Bismuth Quadruple (14 days)]
- Losec 20mg cap (Omeprazole) | كبسولة مرتين يوميًا قبل الأكل بـ 30 دقيقة | 27 ج.م
- Bismuth subsalicylate 120mg tab | 4 قراص يوميًا (2 مرتين) | 8 ج.م
- Metronidazole 500mg tab | قرص 3 مرات يوميًا بعد الأكل | 34 ج.م
- Tetracycline 500mg tab | قرص 4 مرات يوميًا بعد الأكل | 8 ج.م
- OR Bispyller cap (Bismuth + Metronidazole + Tetracycline) | 3 كبسولات، 4 مرات يوميًا لمدة 10 أيام — بديل مجمّع | 800 ج.م

[RX-Protocol 2 — Levofloxacin Triple (14 days)]

⚠️ Repeat urea breath test 4 weeks after finishing
❌ Do NOT skip doses — promotes resistance

❌ Disulfiram-like reaction. Avoid alcohol 48h after last dose.

title: Acute Gastroenteritis
subtitle: Adult patient, less than 14 days of watery diarrhea
content:
[DIAGNOSIS]
- Acute watery diarrhea, less than 14 days duration
- May be associated with nausea, vomiting, colicky abdominal pain
- Fever + blood in stool suggests invasive bacterial cause
- Check hydration status: skin turgor, capillary refill

[INVESTIGATIONS]
- Lab: Electrolytes (Na+/K+ — dehydration), renal function; FBC if bloody diarrhea
- Culture: Stool MC&S if bloody/persistent diarrhea or invasive cause suspected
- Special test: Hydration assessment (skin turgor, capillary refill, urine output)
- Monitor: Fluid intake/output, weight, stool frequency, fever; reassess hydration

[TREATMENT]
- Rehydration is the real treatment, not antibiotics
- Oral rehydration solution after every loose stool
- Antispasmodic for colic, antipyretic if fever present
- Antibiotics only if invasive bacterial cause suspected

[WARNING]
Do not give Loperamide if fever or blood in stool present — risk of toxic megacolon.

- Brufen 400mg tab (Ibuprofen) | قرص 3 مرات يوميًا بعد الأكل | 78 ج.م
- Ciprofloxacin 500mg tab (Ciprofloxacin HCl) | قرص مرتين يوميًا لمدة 5 أيام | 53 ج.م

Ciprofloxacin + QT-prolonging drugs:
⚠️ Increased cardiac risk.

title: GERD & Peptic Ulcer
subtitle: Heartburn, epigastric pain, acid reflux
content:
[DIAGNOSIS]
- Burning epigastric pain / retrosternal burning
- Worse after meals or lying down, relieved partly by antacids
- Alarm features (weight loss, bleeding, dysphagia) need endoscopy

[INVESTIGATIONS]
- Lab: FBC (anaemia from bleeding), LFTs; H. pylori testing if ulcer suspected
- Special test: Endoscopy (OGD) — indicated with alarm features or refractory symptoms
- Monitor: Response to PPI trial, symptom control, red flag symptoms at each visit
- Biopsy: Endoscopic biopsy for H. pylori if ulcer/atrophic changes

[TREATMENT]
- PPIs are prodrugs, activated only in acidic environment
- Must be taken 30–60 min before a meal to work properly
- H2 blockers are a good alternative if PPIs not tolerated

[WARNING]
Alarm signs: dysphagia, weight loss, vomiting blood, black stools — refer for endoscopy.

title: Vomiting
subtitle: Nausea and vomiting from a non-surgical cause
content:
[DIAGNOSIS]
- D2 antagonist: Metoclopramide, Domperidone
- 5HT3 antagonist: Ondansetron, Granisetron
- H1 antihistamine: Meclizine, Cyclizine

[INVESTIGATIONS]
- Lab: Electrolytes (dehydration), renal function, FBS (DKA cause), pregnancy test (female)
- Imaging: Abdominal X-ray/CT if suspected obstruction or surgical cause
- ECG: Baseline if ondansetron used (QT prolongation at high dose)
- Monitor: Hydration status, urine output, response to antiemetic; persistent vomiting review

[TREATMENT]
- Domperidone preferred — does not cross the BBB easily
- Metoclopramide adds central antiemetic effect
- Ondansetron for severe / chemotherapy-related nausea

[WARNING]
Metoclopramide: avoid in patients under 20 — high risk of extrapyramidal symptoms. Ondansetron high dose: prolongs QT interval.

- Motilium 10mg tab (Domperidone) | قرص 3 مرات يوميًا قبل الأكل بنصف ساعة | 100 ج.م
- OR Primperan 10mg tab (Metoclopramide) | قرص 3 مرات يوميًا قبل الأكل | 10.5 ج.م
- Zofran 8mg tab (Ondansetron) | قرص مرتين يوميًا | 364 ج.م

drugInstructions:
⚠️ Metoclopramide: Avoid in patients under 20 — extrapyramidal risk
⚠️ Domperidone: Take 15-30 min before meals
⚠️ Ondansetron: Dissolve under tongue or take with water
✅ Domperidone preferred — does not cross BBB easily
⚠️ If vomiting >48h or blood in vomit → seek urgent care
⚠️ Sip clear fluids in small amounts
❌ Avoid large meals
drugInteractions:
Metoclopramide + SSRIs (Fluoxetine):
⚠️↑ Risk of extrapyramidal symptoms.

Ondansetron + QT-prolonging drugs:
⚠️ Further QT prolongation. ECG monitoring.

Domperidone + CYP3A4 inhibitors (Ketoconazole, Erythromycin):
⚠️↑↑ Domperidone levels → cardiac risk. Avoid.

title: Constipation
subtitle: Infrequent or difficult bowel movements, no organic cause
content:
[DIAGNOSIS]
- Stimulant: Senna, Bisacodyl
- Osmotic: Lactulose, Mg salts, PEG
- Bulk-forming: Bran, Ispaghula

[INVESTIGATIONS]
- Lab: Calcium, TSH, FBS (exclude hypothyroidism, diabetes), renal function, electrolytes
- Special test: Red flags screen (blood in stool, weight loss, new change after 50) → colonoscopy
- Monitor: Stool frequency, response to laxative, electrolyte balance (chronic stimulant use)
- Screen: Medication review for constipating drugs (opioids, iron, calcium blockers)

[TREATMENT]
- Red flags — refer: Blood in stool, unexplained weight loss
- New change in bowel habit after age 50

[WARNING]
Chronic stimulant laxative use risks electrolyte disturbance and bowel dependency — limit to short courses.

⚠️ Increase dietary fibre gradually to avoid bloating

⚠️↑ Risk of electrolyte imbalance — monitor potassium and magnesium.

Bisacodyl + Milk / Antacids:
❌ Reduce bisacodyl absorption — take on empty stomach or 1h apart.

Chronic Stimulant Use:
⚠️ Bowel dependency — limit to short courses, prefer osmotic laxatives long-term.

title: Spastic Colon / IBS
subtitle: Recurrent abdominal pain with altered bowel habit
content:
[DIAGNOSIS]
- Colicky pain: Mebeverine, Trimebutine
- Diarrhea-dominant: Streptoquin, Loperamide with caution
- Constipation-dominant: Lactulose, bulk-forming agents

[INVESTIGATIONS]
- Lab: CBC, TSH, FBS, coeliac serology (tTG-IgA), ESR/CRP — exclude organic causes
- Culture: Stool MC&S if infectious diarrhea suspected
- Special test: IBS diagnostic criteria (Rome IV); colonoscopy if alarm features or age > 50
- Monitor: Stool diary (Bristol scale), symptom frequency, response to antispasmodic

[TREATMENT]
- Small frequent meals, avoid large ones
- Reduce caffeine and stimulants
- Regular physical activity, good sleep

[WARNING]
Rifaximin is not a general IBS treatment — proven role only in IBS-D with suspected bacterial overgrowth.

title: Oral Problems
subtitle: Gingivitis, herpes, thrush, oral sores
content:
[DIAGNOSIS]
- Vesicles around lip: Herpes simplex
- White patches: Mouth thrush
- Painful ulcer, white membrane: Oral sore
- Red swollen gums: Gingivitis

[INVESTIGATIONS]
- Culture: Swab of lesions/vesicles for HSV if herpes suspected; oral swab for candida
- Special test: Full dental examination; biopsy if ulcer persists > 2 weeks
- Monitor: Lesion healing, response to treatment, recurrence (herpes)
- Screen: Blood count if recurrent aphthous ulcers (iron, B12, folate deficiency)

[WARNING]
Ulcer lasting over 2 weeks, recurrent, or with systemic symptoms — think autoimmune cause or refer.

title: Inflammatory Bowel Disease
subtitle: Confirmed UC / Crohn's — supportive role of general practice
content:
[DIAGNOSIS]
- Mesalazine (5-ASA) — first line for mild-moderate UC
- Sulfasalazine — cheaper alternative, more side effects
- Needs endoscopic / pathology confirmation before treatment

[INVESTIGATIONS]
- Biopsy: Endoscopy with colonoscopy and pathology — confirm UC or Crohn's diagnosis
- Lab: FBC (anaemia), ESR/CRP, faecal calprotectin, renal function, LFTs, electrolytes
- Culture: Stool MC&S to exclude infective colitis before starting therapy
- Monitor: Stool frequency, weight, abdominal symptoms, response to mesalazine

[TREATMENT]
- Recognize the pattern and refer to GI specialist
- Supportive: nutrition, symptom monitoring
- Not the setting to start immunosuppressive therapy

[WARNING]
Sulfasalazine reduces folic acid absorption — supplement separately.

title: Liver Support
subtitle: Adjunct supplements — not a substitute for treating the cause
content:
[DIAGNOSIS]
- Silymarin: Regeneration + antioxidant
- Glutathione: Toxin protection
- Lecithin: Removes fat deposits

[INVESTIGATIONS]
- Lab: LFTs (ALT/AST), bilirubin, GGT, viral hepatitis screen (HBsAg, anti-HCV)
- Imaging: Abdominal ultrasound — steatosis, cirrhosis, portal hypertension
- Special test: Fibroscan (liver stiffness) if fibrosis suspected; lipid profile
- Monitor: LFTs, symptom response, alcohol intake, weight (NAFLD)

[TREATMENT]
- These are supportive only
- The underlying cause — virus, fatty liver, toxin — must be diagnosed and treated
